archetype.name: Dual-Threat (scramble-first)
archetype.definition: A passer who wins with accuracy from the pocket and does his real damage when plays break down, turning pressure into scrambles rather than relying on designed runs.

report.headline: Sharper passer than ever, still bleeding sacks, and now without McLaurin
report.take:
Daniels in 2026 is a different passer than the one who struggled through an injury-shortened 2025. His CPOE of 6.44 ranks 6th of 45 and is 9.2 points above last year's, he has not thrown an interception on 116 attempts, and his accuracy has climbed every week: -3.4 CPOE in Week 1, 17.6 at San Francisco in Week 6. The 300-yard game against the league's 9th-ranked defense, with a 8.6% bad-throw rate, was the cleanest he has looked since his rookie year. Still, the passing EPA per dropback (0.034, 24th) sits just under the league average of 0.04. The accuracy is real, but it hasn't turned into efficiency yet.

The gap between how well he throws and what his passing produces comes down to three leaks. The first is sacks: a 7.9% sack rate ranks 32nd, he's taken nine in his last three games, and five of his 33 third-down plays ended in sacks. That helps explain a 30.3% conversion rate on downs averaging 8.8 yards to go. The second is the throws behind the line, which cost his offense -10.1 EPA on 14 attempts and wiped out almost all the value his short game built. The third is game state: his best passing has come trailing by 9+ (0.244 EPA, 19.5 CPOE), while in one-score situations he's at -0.073. Several of those problems belong to the offense around him as much as to him. Washington's hit rate allowed ranks 27th, and screens that lose that much EPA point to design and blocking.

What carries his fantasy line, and a lot of his real value, is the legs. He leads all qualifiers at 53.3 rushing yards a game, and 19 scrambles have produced 212 yards, 10 first downs and 0.846 EPA each. His dropback EPA total of 20.7 dwarfs his passing total of 4.3, and most of that difference is scrambles. The designed runs are a non-factor (4 plays, -0.904 EPA, half stuffed), so this is improvisation, not a run-game package. Sack-proneness has always been part of the trade: his pressure-to-sack rate ranked 54th of 60 as a rookie. This year's 30.3% is actually his best yet, so the high sack rate reflects how often he's pressured more than a new habit of holding the ball.

The outlook just changed. Terry McLaurin is out for the season with a torn patellar tendon, taking 0.661 EPA per target and a chunk of the vertical game with him. The deep ball was already boom-or-bust (29.4% completions on 17 attempts). Stefon Diggs and Chig Okonkwo have been productive, and Antonio Williams has been startling on a tiny sample (1.448 EPA per target on 11 looks). Expect that sample to regress as his role grows. The intermediate game, where he's completing throws at 22.4 points over expected, is what has to carry this passing offense now.

strengths.title: Accuracy jump that keeps building
strengths.body: His CPOE ranks 6th, and the leap from last season is too large and too steady week-to-week to wave off as noise. It shows up most between 10 and 19 air yards, where he's averaging 0.514 EPA. The intermediate sample is only 23 throws, so the exact number will cool, but improving every game against varied defenses suggests a real step forward.

strengths.title: Scrambles that pay for the chaos
strengths.body: Nineteen scrambles for 212 yards and 10 first downs, at 0.846 EPA a scramble, make broken plays his best offense. This is the trait that defined his 891-yard rookie season, so it's who he is, not a hot streak. It also offsets much of what the sacks cost.

strengths.title: Ball security so far
strengths.body: He has no interceptions and no lost fumbles, both ranked 1st. The bad-throw rate has improved slightly and his aggressiveness is in line with past seasons, so he isn't simply dumping the ball off. A zero won't last, but he has cut last year's interception rate to nothing without playing scared.

concerns.title: Sacks are draining drives
concerns.body: His 7.9% sack rate ranks 32nd, and his last three games pushed it to 9.9%. Third down is where it shows: five sacks and -0.169 EPA. Part of it is a line whose hit rate allowed ranks 27th. Part of it is the cost of his extend-and-create style, and his pressure-to-sack rate is actually his career best. That makes this something to manage, not a collapse, but it caps his passing efficiency.

concerns.title: McLaurin gone for the year
concerns.body: McLaurin's 0.661 EPA per target was the best among his regular targets. He was the receiver who made the deep and intermediate shots work. Diggs is a capable lead option, but Williams' 1.448 EPA per target on 11 looks is a sample due for regression, and Burks has been negative. Expect fewer chunk plays and more short work.

concerns.title: Close-game passing lags
concerns.body: With the score within one possession he's at -0.073 EPA a play. His best passing has come trailing by 9+, where defenses are protecting leads. The negative screen game (-10.1 total EPA behind the line) is part of the reason, and that's more scheme and blocking than his arm.

trend.note: His CPOE has risen in each game, from -3.4 to 17.6, and Week 6 at San Francisco was his best passing day. Per-game EPA has bounced around because of sacks, and the 0-3-1 record hides how much better he's throwing.

nextGame.headline: Eagles' weak pass rush targets his biggest weakness
nextGame.body:
Philadelphia's defense ranks 32nd in both hit rate and sack rate. That goes straight at the leak that has held back his passing efficiency, and edge Nolan Smith Jr. is out. The defense is 27th in pass EPA and 31st against the run, and it has given lead receivers 0.54 EPA per target (28th). That's the role Diggs now inherits. Daniels already handled this unit in Week 1 on the road: 3.9 passing EPA, one sack and pressure on only 18.4% of dropbacks. The slot and outside cornerback depth is also thin, with Michael Carter II out and Jakorian Bennett on IR.

The catch is game script and volume. Philadelphia's offense ranks 29th, and it's missing Lane Johnson, center Jake Majors, DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, with Saquon Barkley questionable. Washington is a 4.5-point favorite with a 40.5 total, so a lead that leans the game toward the run could cap his attempts. That shifts value toward his rushing rather than erasing it. On his side, McLaurin's absence matters most. Marcus Mariota's knee affects only the backup spot, and Daniels practiced fully. The early forecast shows gusts to 24 mph with mild sustained wind; check it closer to kickoff, but don't plan around it.

keyMatchups.title: Clean pockets against a dead rush
keyMatchups.body: No defense hits or sacks quarterbacks less often than Philadelphia. If Daniels gets time, his accuracy can show up on third down instead of drives ending in sacks. Watch whether his sack count drops toward his Week 1 level here.

keyMatchups.title: Diggs as the new WR1
keyMatchups.body: With McLaurin out, Diggs becomes the clear top receiver against a defense that has let WR1s beat their usual output by 4 PPR points a game. His 0.601 EPA per target makes him a strong first read.

keyMatchups.title: Depleted Eagles offense shapes script
keyMatchups.body: Philadelphia's offense ranks 29th and is missing two starting linemen and its top two wideouts. A Washington lead would trim pass volume, but it also takes away the trailing-by-9+ passing that has padded his numbers. Run-game efficiency against a 31st-ranked run defense becomes the main way he scores.

nextGame.watch: His sack count. Against the league's weakest pass rush, a multi-sack game would say the problem is him, not the line.

restOfSeason.body:
The parts to trust are the accuracy, the scrambling and the careful decision-making. The CPOE gain has held and grown over four games, and scramble value has been his calling card since 2024. The parts that regress are the zero interceptions, the five red-zone touchdowns on a 45.8% completion rate, and Williams' outsized efficiency. Losing McLaurin should flatten the deep game and keep his yards per attempt modest. Expect something like 190 to 230 passing yards a game rather than a breakout. The rushing floor keeps his fantasy line among the position's best even when the passing is ordinary.

The bigger question is protection. If the sack rate settles nearer his improved pressure-to-sack profile than his last three games, the accuracy should finally show up in EPA, and Washington's offense moves from mid-pack to above average. If not, he stays a dual-threat whose legs cover for a passing game stuck around league average.
swingFactors: Sack rate behind a line allowing frequent hits
How the targets settle without McLaurin
Whether game scripts keep him throwing from behind

confidence.note: Four games, thin splits, and a new receiver group after McLaurin's injury, but the accuracy trend and rushing are consistent with his career.
